notes: Technology is well documented; CCT is not. Wenhui (Aug 2022): about 825,400 road lights, about 85% HPS. The Three-Year Action Plan (2021-2023) aimed to replace about 704,000 HPS with LED; 250,000 were scheduled for 2022; pilots on the Yixian Rd and Tongji Rd elevated roads in June 2022. fx361 (2023): 701,400 HPS (85%) vs 124,000 LED (15%). Gelonghui (loaded): 924,000 road lights at end-2023, about 260,000 converted to LED in 2023. A search snippet attributed to the Shanghai Green Lighting report (NOT verified by loading) gives LED share 21.9% (2021) rising to 83.9% (2024), about 880k LED at end-2024 and about 450k replaced under the three-year plan. Xinmin Evening News via sohu (Sep 2026, loaded): about 977,000 road lights at end-2025. No CCT found in any document. The Shanghai standard DG/TJ08-2214-2024 exists but its text could not be read (garbled PDF). I did not find any written warm or yellow-light policy; that is unverified. Satellite: Liu et al. 2024 (RSE 305:114079, SDGSAT-1 GLI) classified LED vs HPS (OA 89.9%) and reported a 13.09% energy saving versus 42.82% for full conversion; by my arithmetic this implies about 30% of streetlight load had converted by the image date (about 2022). That share is derived, not stated in the paper. Lv et al. 2024 (Applied Energy 355:122355) also classified Shanghai lighting; its numbers were not accessible.

notes: Guangdong provincial LED campaign compilation (June 2013, loaded): by then Dongguan had installed or retrofitted 65,000 LED road lights. Shipai town was the first pilot and had full LED coverage in 2008 (6,198 lamps). Wanjiang subdistrict added or retrofitted 4,070 LED lamps under EMC in 2010, including on National Road 107. Only 3 towns had finished retrofits by mid-2013; 8 had tendered and the rest planned tenders by June 2013. COEMA (Mar 2009): about 5,200 LED lights installed, expanding to 8,700; the Shilong/Shipai demo had 4,100 lamps on 23 streets and 68 km. A search snippet describes these as 'high-power white LED', with no K value. The same 2013 compilation says the Guangshen Expressway retrofit (the expressway runs through Dongguan) replaced about 6,280 250W HPS lamps with 100W LED at a CCT not above 4000K. The total street-light count and current LED share were not found. Early (2008-2013) Chinese LED streetlights were typically cool white (>=5000K), but no document confirms this for Dongguan, so cct_k is left blank.

Foshan municipal government report in the June 2013 Guangdong compilation (loaded): 87,665 LED street lights installed citywide, among the largest in the province. Before unified procurement only 19,000 had been retrofitted; 68,600 more followed within about 7 months (+350%). Chancheng District was the first in the province to use EMC, with 11,000+ LED lights and 54m yuan (alighting 2010, snippet). A search engine summary said Foshan's LED lights were 'CCT <=4000K'. In the source that spec belongs to the Guangshen Expressway project, NOT Foshan, so I did not use it. Total street-light count and current LED share were not found. Left blank for CCT.

cct_range: 3000 (road lighting LED luminaires); 4000 for footbridges, subways and covered walkways; 3000 in 'prestigious' or low-brightness areas
notes: HyD Public Lighting Design Manual (3rd ed., 2016), clause 2.8.1: 'LED luminaires shall comply with IEC 62471 ... Group 1 or Exempt Group and shall have a correlated colour temperature at 3000K.' Clause 7.2.2.2 sets 4000K for footbridge and subway luminaires (3000K in prestigious areas). I did not check whether a newer PLDM edition has changed this. Audit Commission Report No.65 Ch.8 (Oct 2015): the road lighting system used HPS; only 157 LED road lights plus 672 LED tubes on footbridges were on trial as of Aug 2015. HyD LED replacement page (loaded): programme started 2017/18; as of Feb 2025 more than 90% of street lights had been replaced with LED (about 130,500 street lights plus 20,250 structure lights, per a search snippet). About 240,000 lighting facilities in total; expanded programme from 2024/25 with completion expected in 2029 (for all facilities, including sign and structure lights). led_share_pct 90 is a lower bound for street lights, as of Feb 2025.

cct_range: low-CCT 'yellow' LED (K value not stated in sources seen)
spd_hint: LED warm (~3000K assumed from 'yellow LED' policy)
notes: NTPC results site (loaded): all of about 256,000 street lights are LED; about 20,000 are smart lights. Phase 1 (Oct 2020 - Apr 2021) replaced about 42,000 high-failure LEDs, i.e. the earlier 'Energy Bureau project' LED lights from the national MOEA programme. Phase 2 replaced about 214,000 older LED lights at end of service life under the PFI; the project ran 2020-10-10 to 2023-10-09. A search snippet dates Phase 2 to Oct 2023 - Oct 2024, which contradicts the results site. So the city was already essentially all-LED before 2020, and 2020-2023 was a second-generation LED replacement. China Times (2021-05-11; snippet only, page blocked by bot-check), headline 'New Taipei street lights unified to yellow lamps; alleys got darker': in 2014 the city decided to adopt 'energy-saving, low-CCT yellow LED' throughout, so white and yellow would not be mixed. No Kelvin value found; 'yellow' LED in Taiwanese usage is usually about 3000K (possibly 2700K), hence cct_k is left blank. The PFI tender Q&A PDF (loaded) does not state CCT. CTEE (Oct 2024): north-district PFI covers about 120,000 lights.

notes: Ward and city level only. Suginami: 33,309 of 33,925 street lights (about 98%) LED as of 2026-04-01, conversion since FY2017.
